entry.content:

entry.title: IDBDatabase: make the upgrade example work for existing databases
entry.content:
Description

Reworks the onupgradeneeded handler in the IDBDatabase example so it handles upgrades from an older version, not just first-time creation:

  • The handler now checks event.oldVersion and applies each upgrade step the user hasn't had yet. Version 1 creates the toDoList store and its date/time indexes; version 2 adds the notified index to the existing store, which it gets from the upgrade transaction (DBOpenRequest.transaction.objectStore()) instead of calling createObjectStore() again.
  • The open() call asks for version 2 to match.
  • Fixes a node.appendChild typo (the variable is note), plus a missing full stop in a comment.

Motivation

As the issue says, the old handler always called createObjectStore("toDoList"), so it only worked when the database didn't exist yet. Bumping the version for anyone with an existing database threw a ConstraintError and aborted the upgrade. I checked this with fake-indexeddb: after creating the database at version 1, the old handler fails on the upgrade to version 2 with ConstraintError, while the new handler produces the same six indexes both for a fresh install at version 2 and for an upgrade from version 1.

Additional details

IndexedDB spec, IDBVersionChangeEvent.oldVersion (0 for a new database) and IDBOpenDBRequest.transaction during an upgrade.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #26638

entry.title: New guide: Fetch priority
entry.content:
Description

Adds a guide on fetch priority under Web/Performance/Guides, with a sidebar entry and a line on the Performance landing page.

Motivation

#14803 asks for a topic on prioritizing resource requests. There's reference for fetchpriority, the priority option of fetch(), preload and the Priority header, but no page that ties them together. The guide covers how browsers pick a default priority, how resources get discovered, and where each tool fits.

Two things in the issue came out different when I checked them. There's no fetchpriority on <iframe> in the HTML spec or in BCD, and Request has no priority property, only the init option. The page says both.

Additional details

Chrome's defaults come from the table in https://web.dev/articles/fetch-priority and Firefox's from https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/networking/http/prioritization.html. Browser-specific behavior is attributed to the browser, and version numbers are left to the reference pages.

I ran the examples in Chrome 154 against a local server and read each request's priority over the DevTools protocol. They matched what the page says, with one exception: I couldn't get headless Chrome to raise hidden carousel slides to High, so that sentence leans on the web.dev article. Nothing was tested in Firefox or Safari.

The rel="preload" reference page says a preload is "downloaded and cached with a higher priority", which doesn't hold for images in Chrome. I left that page alone here and can send a small follow-up.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #14803

entry.title: New page: `flow-tolerance`
entry.content:
Description

This adds a reference page for the flow-tolerance CSS property, which sets how close the tracks of a grid lanes container must be in length before they count as tied during item placement.

Motivation

The property ships in Safari 26.4 and already has BCD data (css.properties.flow-tolerance), but MDN has no page for it, and the grid lanes guide doesn't mention it.

Additional details

  • Spec: flow-tolerance and the grid lanes placement algorithm, which defines how ties are broken using the auto-placement cursor.
  • I checked the example item heights against the spec algorithm, then rendered the "Try it" demo and the live sample in WebKit. Item placement matches the page text for 0, normal, and infinite.
  • {{cssinfo}} reports a TemplMdnDataMissing flaw because mdn/data has no flow-tolerance entry yet. Recent pages such as column-rule-inset-junction-end and rule-break have the same gap.
  • markdownlint-cli2 and prettier --check report 0 issues, the front-matter linter passes, and I previewed the page with npm start.
  • The issue mentions Chrome Canary support, which BCD doesn't record yet, so the compat table only lists Safari for now.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #45943

entry.title: ci(pr-checks): add aggregate reusable checks
entry.content:
Description

Update PR checks to run through one aggregate workflow.

  • Convert the individual check workflows into reusable workflows.
  • Select checks by changed files and report a single aggregate result.
  • Move the concurrency group to the aggregate workflow, so a new push cancels the whole run.

Motivation

Allow one required status check while keeping individual checks selective.

Additional details

The branch protection ruleset must switch the required status check from Check Redirects / check-redirects to PR checks / all-checks-passed-or-skipped when this merges. Otherwise the old required check stays pending forever and blocks merges.

Check names in the PR UI change to PR checks / <check> / <job> (e.g. PR checks / lint_content / lint).

entry.title: docs: clarify user-origin CSS priority in tabs.insertCSS
entry.content:
Description

Clarify that normal CSS injected with tabs.insertCSS({ cssOrigin: "user" }) does not override website author styles, while user-origin declarations marked !important do.

Motivation

The current wording suggests that selecting "user" alone prevents websites from overriding injected CSS. This can mislead extension authors who omit !important.

Additional details

The CSS Cascade Level 5 specification ranks normal author declarations above normal user declarations, and important user declarations above important author declarations.

Documentation-only change. Verified with git diff --check.

Related issues and pull requests

Relates to #43033.

entry.title: IDBFactory.deleteDatabase(): explain what happens while a deletion is blocked
entry.content:
Description

Adds two things to IDBFactory.deleteDatabase():

  • A paragraph on what happens while a deletion is blocked: open connections keep working until they are closed, and later open() / deleteDatabase() requests for the same database wait behind the pending deletion.
  • A "Handling a blocked deletion" example that listens for blocked alongside success.

Motivation

#44350 already explains why a deletion gets blocked and how to unblock it. Readers still had to work out on their own what the blocked state means for existing connections and for new requests (points 3 and 4 of the issue), and the page had no example that handles blocked.

Additional details

IndexedDB spec: deleting a database and opening a database both add the request to the connection queue for the storage key and name, and wait for earlier requests in that queue. Firefox report that prompted the issue: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2006245

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #42779
Relates to #44350
